reason: Mechanism verified verbatim. ConfigManager.loadFromFile() (1360-1933) reaches the early return at 1387-1394 on unusable/ABSENT/read-only, and the last executable statement before `return false` is `lastSavedSnapshot = activeConfig.snapshot()` (1393). snapshot() is a genuine deep copy (GameConfig.java:594-668, deep-copies monsters/waves/defaultWave/starterKit), so this is not aliasing: lastSavedSnapshot becomes a separate object holding the modified in-memory values, and hasUnsavedChanges() (307-313) then compares activeConfig.snapshot() against an equal copy and returns false (or true only if loadTimeNormalizationPending survived, since that flag is cleared only on the success path at 1408). MainConfigMenu.java:96 is the only consumer, so the re-render after reopen() (line 121/162 -> AbstractConfigMenu.java:56-63) really switches slot 45 from LIME_WOOL save to GREEN_WOOL "Config is up to date" (126-128), and the revert button's `if (configManager.hasUnsavedChanges())` at 134 becomes a no-op. Reachable from /hilltop config -> reload (MainConfigMenu:151) and from /hilltop reloadconfig (HilltopCommandHandler.java:422) when the file is still corrupt or absent after quarantine. Severity, however, is overstated: in the read-only trigger the save would have failed anyway (saveToFile returns false immediately at ConfigManager.java:796 when !settingsGate.writable()), and reloadDisplay/reloadconfig rebuiling activeConfig from disk (1405) discards those edits regardless, so no additional data loss is caused by the flag itself; the real damage is a false "up to date/no save needed" indicator, a suppressed retry, and an unusable revert, with the failure still announced (config.menu.main.reload-failed, messages.yml:635 / config-reload-failed:23). The only case where a working retry is actually lost is an externally deleted game-settings.yml (Status.ABSENT with a writable gate), where saveToFile would have recreated the file successfully.
